snippets.back: An acceptable United States birth certificate must be certified, bear a raised seal and come from an authorized government agency; hospital and baptismal certificates do not qualify.

In an emergency, a driver of any age may use a cell phone or mobile electronic device to call police or fire departments, an ambulance service, a hospital, a health clinic, a physician's office, or an emergency response operator, while peace officers, firefighters, and ambulance drivers eighteen or older may use handheld devices.
Wallet birth cards and hospital birth announcements or records are unacceptable substitutes for the required birth certificate.
Blue-and-white service signs direct travelers to facilities such as fuel, food, lodging, a hospital or camping.
Service signs point to rest areas, fuel, campgrounds, and hospitals.
A US birth certificate used as identity proof must be an original or certified copy issued by a government agency, and unofficial hospital birth certificates are not accepted.
Service signs use a blue background with white letters or symbols for facilities such as fuel, lodging, hospitals and rest areas.
Guide signs in green, brown, or blue squares and rectangles point to crossing roads, towns, sights, hospitals, fuel, food, and lodging.
